title_vi: Hồi ký của người chết Brás Cubas
translation_direction: pt → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Portuguese electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Machado’s dry, digressive, ironic dead narrator, the short capricious chapters and the direct addresses to the reader are kept in light, lucid Vietnamese without explaining the jokes.
decisions.rationale: The novel’s effect is tone and the rhythm of its brevity.

decisions.decision: The dot-and-shape passages (and the Latin ‘arma virumque cano’) are copied verbatim with their spacing and line breaks.
decisions.rationale: They are visual jokes, not text.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘Dr. Villaça’, a lettered graduate and poet, was rendered as a medical physician (‘bác sĩ’); ‘doutor’ is now treated as an honorific by context throughout.
‘Desci da Tijuca’ (came down from Tijuca) was rendered with the direction inverted; now ‘tôi từ Tijuca xuống’.
‘Entristecer-me’ was rendered with the polarity inverted (‘không buồn’); corrected.
‘Doutor’ was rendered ‘bác sĩ’ for a graduate who is not a physician; corrected, and the same title in 580 unified.

Sabina’s and Cotrim’s kinship and seniority forms toward Brás were inconsistent across units; Sabina is Brás’s younger sister, Cotrim ‘em rể’ to him and Brás ‘anh vợ’ to Cotrim, applied in all slices.
The hedged ‘Prazer é muito’ was rendered ‘Khoái thì nhiều’, losing the hedge; corrected.
‘Dieta germanica’ (the German Diet) was misread; corrected during the fix round.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: Hồi ký của người chết Brás Cubas
glossary.rationale: ‘Memórias póstumas’ are memoirs written after death.

glossary.draft_rendering: ông / cậu / ngài by context; bác sĩ only for a physician
glossary.rationale: In the 1880s ‘doutor’ is an honorific for any graduate.

glossary.draft_rendering: Sabina: em gái of Brás; Cotrim: em rể to Brás, Brás anh vợ to Cotrim
glossary.rationale: One kinship system across the book.

glossary.source_term: typographic passages (dots, Virgilio shape, arma virumque cano)
glossary.rationale: They are not translatable and carry no words to render.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #54829, an electronic transcription of Memorias Posthumas de Braz Cubas by Machado de Assis (Rio de Janeiro: Typographia Nacional, 1881). The text was not collated with the printed edition and its orthography is the original’s, not modern Portuguese.

unresolved_questions.explanation: ‘Biển xanh’ in unit 348 where the source means the sky.
‘Não serias capaz’ is rendered ‘không dám’, a shade off.

title_review.target_title: Hồi ký của người chết Brás Cubas
title_review.rationale: The title is translated as ‘Hồi ký của người chết Brás Cubas’; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening address: the author hopes for fewer readers than Stendhal’s hundred.
The last unit: ‘Não tive filhos, não transmitti a nenhuma creatura o legado da nossa miseria.’
